scope.population: 12 cells over coin x horizon x wallet floor, of which 12 were testable; wallets per cell run 328 to 1,168 at the eligibility floors K = [50, 100] fills in EACH half. Built from 2,480,267 collapsed taker fills
scope.window: early [4, 5, 6, 7, 8] / late [9, 10, 11, 12, 13], day-of-month, out of the 10 days requested; 24 hours per day

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

settings_fingerprint.early_late_split: inherited from i3, which cuts by settings.split_early_late: early [4, 5, 6, 7, 8], late [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]
settings_fingerprint.fold_seed_sweep: 1..40, a separate seed family from master_seed; see seed_robustness
settings_fingerprint.overrides_note: master_seed 20260619 is i3's, re-used so the folds and the placebo are identical to the trade-tape run, and it is not settings.MASTER_SEED 20260620; n_perm is the declared budget 2000, read from settings.py through i3 and no longer typed, so a p at 0.000500 is the floor and is a bound rather than a measurement, which placebo_p_is_floor records per cell; no bootstrap is drawn, so n_boot does not apply; rank_floor_fills (50, 100) is i3's per-half eligibility floor, not the declared single 50; the halves are cut by the span and rule i3 resolves, which is settings.split_early_late over the days its inputs carry; whales are dropped by NOTIONAL; the fold-seed sweep draws 40 further seeds that vary ONLY which wallets land in which fold

object: I3-BOOK - is per-counterparty toxicity recoverable from the FULL PUBLIC ORDER BOOK (not only the trade tape)?

test_design.p_floor_note: 2000 draws cannot express a p below 0.000500; every cell carries placebo_p_is_floor saying whether its p is a measurement or that floor
test_design.markout_reference: BOOK MID (mo10_mid primary at the headline window 10s, mo60_mid secondary at the companion window 60s; both column names built from settings.py, neither typed here)
test_design.settings_fingerprint_note: in _meta.settings_fingerprint; the population, window and coins are in _meta.scope
test_design.public_info_set: TRADE TAPE (VPIN / signed-flow imbalance / mean size / trade intensity) PLUS the FULL PUBLIC L2 BOOK features ['ofi', 'micro_dev_bps', 'book_vpin', 'qimb_1', 'qimb_5', 'qimb_10', 'depth_bid_5bps', 'depth_ask_5bps', 'depth_bid_10bps', 'depth_ask_10bps'] (OFI, multi-level queue imbalance, book-VPIN, delta-microprice, depth within k bps). NO counterparty identity in any anonymous predictor.
test_design.claim: if the counterparty history FE STILL adds OUT-OF-SAMPLE lift over this FULL PUBLIC info set (positive incremental R^2, small placebo p, FDR survival, whale-robust), per-counterparty toxicity is NOT recoverable from the public book and needs on-chain identity.
test_design.stage2_entry_timestamp_source: cached fill timestamps (notebook_fills.npz), row-checked against the mid intermediate; no raw re-walk

by_coin.interpretation: INCONCLUSIVE/UNDERPOWERED, not a recoverability finding: incremental R^2 -0.0038 <= 0 while incremental Spearman +0.0029 > 0. The positive rank lift means the counterparty FE still orders future toxicity out of sample over the public book; the non-positive R^2 is a level-fit artefact. Do NOT read this cell as the public book recovering toxicity.

family.method: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the cell family (coin x horizon x K)
family.procedure_note: sort ascending, q_(i) = p_(i) * m / i, running minimum from the largest p downward, clipped to 1; NaN p-values are carried through and excluded from the family size
family.threshold_meaning: the p-value cutoff actually applied: the largest rank k with p_(k) <= k*alpha/m, times alpha/m. With no rejection it is the rank-one bar the best cell failed

budget_check.note: a budget whose floor sits above the rank-one threshold cannot produce a significant corrected result however strong the effect is

family.floor_note: a cell whose p sits on the 2000-draw floor 0.000500 says only that no draw beat the observed lift; its q inherits that and is not evidence of a smaller p

seed_robustness.method: re-score each cell over independent k-fold splits, varying only the fold seed; everything upstream of the split is deterministic
seed_robustness.stored_seed_rule: np.random.default_rng(RNG_SEED + K + horizon_s), the single draw reported in by_coin / pooled
seed_robustness.reporting_rule: quote the median with its range, not the single stored draw; for the coin comparison quote the paired difference
seed_robustness.scope_of_variation: This sweep varies ONE thing: which wallets land in which fold. The wallet set, the features and the targets are the same in every draw, so these ranges measure sensitivity to the fold split and NOTHING ELSE. They are NOT confidence intervals and NOT sampling uncertainty about a population, because the draws re-split the same data rather than resampling new data. For the same reason a count like 40 out of 40 seeds is not a p-value and must not be reported as one; the draws are not independent evidence. Sampling uncertainty is addressed separately by the label-permutation placebo (placebo_p) and the whale-drop check.
seed_robustness.paired_note: per-seed difference with the same fold seed on both coins, so shared fold noise cancels; this is the number that answers whether the coins differ rather than whether one draw happened to. Read it as: across every fold split tried, the ETH increment stayed above the BTC increment by about this much. See scope_of_variation for what the interval is and is not.

headline_by_coin.rationale: PRIMARY REPORTED RESULT. Per-coin incremental OOS lift at the 10s K=50 book-mid cell. The coins have OPPOSITE book-recoverability - the public book leaves ETH toxicity almost unrecovered (book-blind) but largely recovers BTC toxicity - so this is reported PER COIN and never pooled. The incremental_oos_r2 shown here is ONE fold split (the paper's 0.47 ETH / 0.06 BTC are these stored draws); seed_robustness carries the median and the range over the fold-seed sweep, and its reporting_rule is to quote that median with its range rather than a single draw. Read the two together.

headline.diagnostic_note: POOLED IS A DIAGNOSTIC ONLY - report headline_by_coin. The coins have opposite book-recoverability (ETH book-blind ~0.47, BTC book-recovers ~0.06); pooling averages them into a number describing neither coin. Per reverification: never pool.
headline.rationale: Pooled book-mid cell, retained as a DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. Pooling averages ETH's book-blind regime with BTC's book-recovered regime into a single value that describes neither coin; cite headline_by_coin instead.
